plugins.name: @denext/avif
plugins.title: @denext/avif
plugins.blurb: A Deno-native AVIF encoder — denext's first-party, zero-npm replacement for the @jsquash/avif peer codec its image optimizer used to lazily import.

plugins.name: @denext/backend
plugins.title: @denext/backend
plugins.blurb: Backend services inside your denext app, as one opt-in plugin: no hosted service, nothing to run beside it.

storage.description: File storage: a driver and the buckets it serves.

init.description: Called once at plugin setup with the project root (resolve relative paths against it).

put.description: Store an object. The stream errors when the body breaks a rule; the driver then stores nothing.

get.description: Read an object (a range of it), or `null` when it does not exist.

head.description: An object's info, or `null` when it does not exist.

remove.description: Delete an object (no error when it does not exist).

list.description: One page of the objects whose key starts with `prefix`, in key order.

direct.description: Direct-to-store URLs, when the store serves clients itself (S3).

createMultipart.description: Start a multipart upload; returns its upload id.

presignPart.description: A presigned PUT for one part (1-based).

completeMultipart.description: Assemble the uploaded parts into the object.

abortMultipart.description: Abandon a multipart upload and free its parts.

buckets.description: The buckets, by name (lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`).

public.description: Anyone may download (no signature, no authorize call), and download URLs are stable and cacheable. Uploads, deletes and listings still need authorize. Default `false`.

maxBytes.description: Largest object accepted, in bytes (default 50 MiB).

mime.description: Allowed content types — exact (`application/pdf`) or `type/*` (`image/*`). Checked on every upload; a declared raster image is also sniffed from its first bytes and must be what it claims. Omitted: any type.

authorize.description: Decide one operation for the current request. Runs whenever a storage call is made inside a request (the plugin's endpoints, and the server API called from a route handler, Server Action or page); a call outside any request (a task, a script) is trusted and skips it. Absent, every operation is denied — except downloads from a public bucket.

secret.description: The HMAC secret (≥ 32 characters) for the plugin's signed URLs and upload tokens — or a list, current first, to rotate one out. Default: `DENEXT_STORAGE_SECRET`; under `denext dev` a random per-process secret when neither is set.

multipartThreshold.description: Uploads larger than this go multipart, when the driver supports it (default 64 MiB).

partSize.description: Multipart part size in bytes (default 16 MiB, at least 5 MiB).

postgres.description: Postgres: the app's database, as `db()` from `@denext/backend/server` (and denext auth's, with `adapter: backendAuthAdapter()`). `{}` reads `DATABASE_URL`.

url.description: A `postgres://` URL (default: `DATABASE_URL`), opened with `Deno.SQL` — the Postgres client built into denext's Deno runtime — and closed when the server drains.

sql.description: A client to use instead of `url`: any `SqlClient` (on stock Deno, `fromPostgresJs(postgres(url))` with the npm `postgres` package). It is never closed by the plugin.

rls.description: Row-level security: `db()` runs every query as `anon` or `authenticated` with the request's claims, so Supabase-style policies apply. The roles and `auth.*` functions are created by a migration on first use unless `migrate: false`.

migrate.description: Apply the `backend_rls_0001` migration (the `anon` / `authenticated` roles, their grant to the connecting role, and the `auth.*` functions) on the first scoped query (default `true`). `false` when a DBA applies rlsSetupSql instead.

claims.description: Extra claims for a signed-in user's `request.jwt.claims` (read in SQL with `auth.jwt() ->> 'tenant'`). Merged over denext's own; `sub`, `role` and `email` cannot be overridden.

realtime.description: Realtime from the database: tables whose inserts, updates and deletes reach `useTableChanges` subscribers (each re-read under that subscriber's row-level security) and `onTableChange` hooks. Needs `postgres`.

tables.description: The tables to send changes from, by name: `{ notes: { events: ["insert"], key: "id" } }`.

events.description: The changes to send (default all three: `["insert", "update", "delete"]`).

key.description: The key column a change is identified by (default `"id"`).

schema.description: The table's schema (default: the connection's search path).

revalidate.description: Also `revalidateTag("table:<name>")` once per burst of changes, so `<Live>`, `useLive`, `useApi({ tags })` and `defineSubscription({ tags })` watchers of that tag are pushed (default `false`).

migrate.description: Install the triggers by migration (recorded in `backend_migrations`) the first time realtime is used (default `true`). `false` when a database administrator applies realtimeSetupSql instead.

maxSubscribers.description: Subscriptions held at once on one server instance (default 10 000).

maxTrackedKeys.description: Keys tracked per subscription, so a delete reaches only subscribers who could see the row (default 10 000); see the docs for what happens past it.

plugins.name: @denext/content-collections
plugins.title: @denext/content-collections
plugins.blurb: A typed, validated, queryable content layer for denext apps — MD/MDX/YAML/JSON, in the spirit of Astro's Content Layer and Nuxt Content.

watch.description: Glob patterns (relative to the project root) whose changes regenerate the store + types in `denext dev`. Defaults to `content.config.ts` and a `content/**` tree; override if your content lives elsewhere.

plugins.name: @denext/effect
plugins.title: @denext/effect
plugins.blurb: First-class Effect support for denext. Run an Effect from a Server Component, route handler, or Server Action and get typed errors, dependency injection (services from a Layer), structured…

layer.description: An app `Layer` providing the services your Effects require (its requirements must be `never`). The plugin builds a memoized runtime from it and disposes it on shutdown; the ambient runEffect/runEffectExit then resolve those services at run time.

plugins.name: @denext/graphql
plugins.title: @denext/graphql
plugins.blurb: A GraphQL endpoint for a denext app, as a plugin. It mounts a GraphQL Yoga server at /graphql, bridges subscriptions onto denext channels (the app's push primitive — no second event bus, no separate…

path.description: Where the endpoint is mounted (default `/graphql`, app-relative: `basePath` is already stripped).

graphiql.description: Serve GraphiQL on a browser `GET` (default: dev only).

introspection.description: Answer introspection queries (default: dev only — production hides the type graph).

maxBodyBytes.description: Max request body in bytes (default 1 MiB, like a route handler; over → 413).

maxDepth.description: Reject a query nested deeper than this many selection levels — a cheap guard against the DoS where a small deeply-nested query over a cyclic type relation exhausts CPU/memory (the body cap allows thousands of levels). Default 12; `false` disables it. Raise it for a schema with legitimately deep trees.

maxCost.description: Reject a query whose estimated **cost** exceeds this budget — the guard against the *multiplicative* DoS a depth limit misses: `users(first: 1000) { posts(first: 1000) { … } }` is shallow but fans out to a million resolver calls. Cost is estimated over the AST (no schema or resolver run): each field costs CostOptions.fieldCost (default 1), and a field carrying a pagination argument (`first`/`last`/`limit` by default) multiplies its children's cost by that integer. Default `false` (off — `maxDepth` stays the on-by-default guard); set a number (a budget of ~1000 suits most apps) to enable it. The check runs at execute time, so a page size passed as a **variable** (`first: $n`) is counted at its **actual** value — a variable can't smuggle a large page past the budget. With Yoga `batching` enabled the budget is per-operation, so an N-operation batch may cost up to N×.

costOptions.description: Tune the GraphqlOptions.maxCost estimate (field weight, which args multiply).

fieldCost.description: Cost charged for each field selected (default `1`).

listMultiplierArgs.description: Argument names whose integer value multiplies a field's subtree cost (default `["first", "last", "limit"]`).

defaultMultiplier.description: Multiplier used for a pagination field when its size is a variable or absent (default `1`).

requireSameOrigin.description: Require the same-origin proof denext applies to every state-changing RPC (Server Actions, the typed-API batch) on non-GET requests: a cross-site `<form>` or fetch is refused with 403 before Yoga parses it. Default `true`. Turn off only for a public, cookie-free API — resolvers run in the viewer's session, so a mutation reached cross-site is a CSRF.

allowedOrigins.description: Extra origins (`https://app.example.com`) allowed to call mutations, beyond the request's own host.

context.description: Build the per-request context your resolvers receive (merged with Yoga's).

yoga.description: Further Yoga options: `plugins`, `maskedErrors`, `cors`, `batching`, `logging`, … Note `cors` defaults to OFF here (Yoga's own default reflects any `Origin` with credentials); set `cors: { origin: [...] }` to open the endpoint to named sites.

outFile.description: The SDL file `denext build` writes into the output directory (default `schema.graphql`); `false` skips it.

plugins.name: @denext/htmx
plugins.title: @denext/htmx
plugins.blurb: First-class htmx support for denext, shipped as a denext plugin. Add it, drop <Htmx/> in your layout, and every hx-* attribute just works — server-rendered verbatim, 0 KB of denext client JS on pages…

path.description: Override the URL the runtime is served from. Defaults to HTMX_RUNTIME_PATH. App-relative: the pipeline strips the project's `basePath` before a plugin sees a request (the browser-facing `<Htmx/>` `src` keeps it).

plugins.name: @denext/lightningcss
plugins.title: @denext/lightningcss
plugins.blurb: A Deno-native WebAssembly build of the lightningcss transform subset denext's CSS pipeline uses.

plugins.name: @denext/og
plugins.title: @denext/og

plugins.name: @denext/openapi
plugins.title: @denext/openapi
plugins.blurb: An OpenAPI 3.1 document and a docs page for a denext app, derived from the defineApi definitions its route handlers already carry.

path.description: Where the document is served (default `/openapi.json`, app-relative: `basePath` is already stripped).

docs.description: Where the docs page is served (default `/docs`, app-relative); `false` disables it.

ui.description: The docs renderer: `builtin` (server-rendered, no JavaScript, strict-CSP clean — the default), `scalar` or `swagger` (interactive, loaded from a CDN).

cdn.description: Override the CDN URL for `scalar` (script URL) or `swagger` (dist base URL).

info.description: The document's `info` (defaults: the project directory's name, version `0.0.0`).

toJsonSchema.description: Describe validators the built-in detection cannot (consulted first).

include.description: Keep a route in the document (default: every API route).

tags.description: Tag an operation (default: the first path segment after `/api`).

securitySchemes.description: Security schemes the document advertises (→ `components.securitySchemes`). Swagger UI and Scalar render an "Authorize" button from these, so a token is entered once and sent with each request. E.g. `{ bearerAuth: { type: "http", scheme: "bearer" } }`.

security.description: Which scheme(s) an operation requires. An **array** is a document-wide default; a **function** is applied per route — return `[{ bearerAuth: [] }]` to require it, `[]` for a public route (e.g. `/api/login`), or `undefined` to leave it at the document default. This is DOCUMENTATION only — enforce the token with route middleware (`createApi().use(...)`).

expose.description: When the live endpoints are served. `"always"` (default) serves `/openapi.json` and `/docs` in every mode — the zero-config default, since a document describing your own API is usually fine to expose. `"dev"` serves them only under `denext dev` (like GraphiQL), so production reveals no route/schema map. Either way authorize still applies.

authorize.description: Gate the live endpoints. Return `false` to hide them from a request (the app's own 404 answers — no distinguishable "forbidden"). Runs after expose. Default: open.

outFile.description: The file `denext build` writes into the output directory (default `openapi.json`); `false` skips the build step.

plugins.name: @denext/pages-router
plugins.title: @denext/pages-router
plugins.blurb: A Next.js Pages Router for denext, shipped as a first-party plugin. Drop it into your denext.config.ts and a pages/ tree renders alongside your App Router app/ routes — App Router routes always win,…

dir.description: Absolute or project-relative path to the pages directory. Defaults to auto-detecting `pages/` then `src/pages/` under the project root.

plugins.name: @denext/react-router
plugins.title: @denext/react-router
plugins.blurb: Run a React Router v7 framework-mode app on denext — with your app's source unchanged.

appDirectory.description: The RR app directory relative to the project (default: `react-router.config.ts`'s `appDirectory`, else `app`).

routesFile.description: The routes config module relative to the app directory (default `routes.ts`).
